rulers.name: Geoffrey V Plantagenet
rulers.title: Count of Maine (1126), of Anjou and Maine (from 1129), Duke of Normandy (from summer 1144)
rulers.note: Ruled to his death on 7 September 1151; the dossier ends in 1146 with Cliopatria's row.

keyframe_review.note: 26,690 km2 for 1126-1138: Anjou (31 of 31 cells), Maine (79%) and Touraine (88%) by gazetteer overlap, the same polygon as the County of Anjou row of 1111-1125. The page says Geoffrey was 'count of Anjou and Maine by inheritance from 1129'; it gives no area.

26,690 km2 for 1139-1146, identical to the 1126 shape (the split at 1139 is a Cliopatria artefact). The shape has no Normandy (0% of the gazetteer's Normandy), although the page has Geoffrey holding Normandy west and south of the Seine by 1142-1143 and Rouen on 14 January 1144 with the duke's title in summer 1144; Cliopatria draws Normandy in Norman England to 1146 and in the Angevin Empire from 1147. Normandy from January 1144 is the Angevin Empire dossier's, so the shape stands here.

region.text: Anjou, Maine and Touraine: the lands of Fulk V and Geoffrey

ledger.note: 1126: Geoffrey Plantagenet is Count of Maine, and of Anjou from 1129. The page's succession table lists him as Count of Maine from 1126; the text says he was 'count of Anjou and Maine by inheritance from 1129', after the marriage of 1128 (he was knighted by Henry I on 10 June 1128): 'The year after the marriage, Geoffrey's father, Fulk, left on crusade for Jerusalem.' The year 1126 is also where Cliopatria's row begins; the land is the Cliopatria shape.

region.text: Normandy west and south of the Seine, which Geoffrey secured by 1143

ledger.note: 1135: Geoffrey backs Matilda's entry into Normandy after Henry I's death, opening the Anjou-Normandy war for the Norman lands west and south of the Seine. The page gives 1135 for the entry and no dates for later invasions (1136, 1138); the ground held is the researcher's reading of the page's statement that in 1142-1143 Geoffrey secured all of Normandy west and south of the Seine.

region.text: Normandy, entered at Rouen on 14 January 1144

ledger.note: 14 January 1144: Geoffrey crosses the Seine and enters Rouen, and takes the title Duke of Normandy in the summer of 1144 ('on 14 January 1144, he crossed the Seine and entered Rouen'). The Angevin Empire dossier (eu-11) carries Normandy from January 1144, so no gain of Normandy is recorded here to avoid a double claim.

1146: the Angevins' land continues unchanged as the Angevin Empire row from 1147. Page silent on 1146 (Geoffrey died on 7 September 1151, at Château-du-Loir, and ceded Normandy to Henry in 1149-1150); the end follows Cliopatria's row and the eu-11 dossier's 1147 merge.

wars.name: The Anarchy (Geoffrey of Anjou's conquest of Normandy)

zones.text: Normandy: the west and south of the Seine by 1143, Rouen on 14 January 1144

wars.outcome: Geoffrey secured Normandy west and south of the Seine in 1142-1143, entered Rouen on 14 January 1144 and took the duke's title in summer 1144; he ceded the duchy to his son Henry in 1149 (Louis VII ratified it in 1150).
wars.note: The Anarchy page was not opened (page budget); the war's name is the usual one and every fact is from the Geoffrey page.

notes:
Written for eu-10-e from two pages (budget 1-2): the Wikipedia page 'Angevin' that Cliopatria cites is a disambiguation page with no history, so the dated facts come from the Geoffrey Plantagenet page. The row 'Angevins' (1126-1146) is the same polygon (26,690 km2: Anjou, Maine and Touraine) as the County of Anjou rows of 1056-1065 and 1111-1125; the county-of-anjou dossier calls it a dormant span 1126-1289 and the Angevin Empire dossier (eu-11) merges it in 1147. This dossier is therefore the county of Anjou under Geoffrey (and his father Fulk V until 1129) drawn under the dynasty's name; whether it should be a separate state or a span of county-of-anjou is for the orchestrator (the Anjou dossier's own note offers both).
NORMANDY: the page has Geoffrey holding Normandy west and south of the Seine by 1142-1143, Rouen on 14 January 1144 and the title Duke of Normandy in summer 1144, but the Angevin Empire dossier starts in January 1144 with Normandy, and Cliopatria puts Normandy in Norman England until 1146; this dossier records only the contest (1135-1144) to avoid a double claim. A gap-filler should check that the compile draws Normandy 1144-1146 from the Angevin Empire dossier.
NOT DONE (page silent): no area on either page; Fulk V's reign (to 1129) and Maine's recovery (1110, in the county-of-anjou dossier) are not on the pages opened; the capital is not on any page opened. The Angevins' wikidata item Q81133615 is Cliopatria's, not checked.
